headline: The two questions that mattered most came back clean. The pii_ceiling client_identified fence on CLIENT_LIST is INTACT, verified six independent ways, and EC-22 creates NO third floor reduction — 0C.32 still declares exactly two. Gate 5 is recomputable and Gate 6 executable.
loadBearingFinding: The ARTIFACT.3 collision. Section 2.6.22 already declares ARTIFACT.1-.4, and its ARTIFACT.3 is a PII clause (contains_pii stated before fetch; pii_ceiling applies). EC-21 introduced a second rule under that number, one clause above the CLIENT.2 collision EC-22 fixed. The lens labelled it independent-pre-existing relative to EC-22; it is NOT independent — section 2.6.22 is body text this cycle never edited, so the collision exists only because EC-21 added the clause. Therefore it is a caused-by-repair defect, repaired as EC-23 (renumbered ARTIFACT.5), not a STOP condition.

causedByEc22.clause: Repair L — §0C.28-sexies's refSet block (line 2968) vs §1.9 H1 (lines 3749-3762)
causedByEc22.consequence: The repair was never effected where it must live. §1.9 H1's body_hash input list is closed and unchanged — contract, kind, body_version, body, cell_index_digest, provenance, limitations, intents.map(stripIntentToken), presentation — and no clause in §0-C amends it; the entire amendment is one sentence inside a // comment ('§1.9 H1's term list gains render.render_tier'). The contract now asserts, in a comment, a property of another section that that section does not have, and that comment is the sole ground offered for refSet taking the fitted tier safely: an envelope whose sealed reading_order was derived at one tier is not hash-bound to that tier. Two things make this sharper than a drafting slip. First, the adjacent repair C rules exactly this failure a defect in terms ('It is DECLARED, not described in a comment — the first draft left it commented out, which is the same left in a code comment only failure §0C.28-sexies item 3 rules a defect'). Second, the parallel amendment in the same block — §1.1.1's render row moving to EP-FIT — IS written as a normative ruling in running text ('Amended to at EP-FIT, attached to the envelope before EP-MINT seals'), which is why that one governs by §0C.2 and this one does not.
causedByEc22.fix: Promote the sentence out of the comment into a ruling in §0C.28-sexies, in the same form as the render-row amendment, and add the matching row to §0C.13: '§1.9 H1 is amended. body_hash's term list gains render.render_tier — that field alone, never the whole RenderReceipt, because R3.3.6 appends target_classes at delivery, after the seal. Mechanism: stableActionJson over the amended term list. Evaluation point: EP-MINT.' Leave the existing comment as commentary.

causedByEc22.consequence: The edit inserted the filtered restatement without removing the phrase it replaced, leaving: 'per-kind membership is what KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths produces **what KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths produces, filtered so that no {k:'intent'} ref names an intent absent from emitted (EC-21), plus every emitted intent not already denoted by a produced ref, in emitted order**'. The left conjunct now appears twice, once unfiltered and once filtered. Read literally, the unfiltered phrase is the predicate of the sentence and the bolded phrase a fragment — which reinstates the exact 'two answers standing side by side' defect EC-17 exists to remove, inside EC-17's own ruling. Before EC-22 the sentence was grammatical ('produces plus every emitted intent not already denoted…').
causedByEc22.fix: Strike the first occurrence, so the sentence reads '…and per-kind membership is **what KIND_REGISTRY[kind].interactive_paths produces, filtered so that no {k:'intent'} ref names an intent absent from emitted (EC-21), plus every emitted intent not already denoted by a produced ref, in emitted order (EC-18 item 2 as amended by EC-20 and EC-21)** — which is what K22's mechanism already performs…'.

causedByEc22.clause: Repairs E + F — §0C.22-quinquies's CLIENT_LIST row and §0C.22-undecies's selection rule (lines 2331-2344, 2353)
causedByEc22.consequence: The CLIENT_LIST suffix is keyed intent:primary, and the crossing pointer now refuses the envelope at EP-MINT when no bulk_intents entry's handle equals ref.id. Two gaps follow. (1) Unscoped refusal: nothing restricts role 'primary' on a CLIENT_LIST to bulk intents — §3.1 lets a composer pick any of the eight roles, and EC-18(2) appends a {k:'intent'} ref to reading_order for every emitted intent not already denoted, which on CLIENT_LIST includes its row intents (denoted only by {k:'row'} refs) and any page intent. If a composer mints one of those role 'primary', A-2 applies the CLIENT_LIST row to it, the pointer matches no bulk entry, and a conforming envelope is refused. The refusal was written to stop a neighbouring entry's audience_size being rendered; applied to a control the column never scoped, the correct outcome is the declared default. The sibling clause APPROVAL.4 saw this and closed it ('an APPROVAL body mints exactly one role primary intent'); CLIENT.3 has no such conjunct. (2) No uniqueness: the rule refuses on zero matches but says nothing about two, while S0.29 expressly contemplates several elements naming one envelope-level intent and names bulk_intents[].intent_token in that list — so two entries sharing one intent_ref is a shape the contract admits, silently re-opening the N-valued pointer this repair exists to close.
causedByEc22.fix: One conjunct on each, in CLIENT.3: '…Every bulk_intents[] entry is role primary, no two entries carry the same intent handle, and no other emitted intent on a CLIENT_LIST body carries role primary.' That makes the selection single-valued and makes §0C.22-undecies's EP-MINT refusal unreachable for a conforming envelope, which is what a fail-closed rule should be.

causedByEc22.clause: Repair D — A-2 as amended, §0C.22 (lines 2050-2052), against §0C.22-quinquies's column type (line 2280)
causedByEc22.consequence: A-2 now claims 'every argument bound, none free', but only two of three are. suffix is bound by prose — 'the entry §4.8.2's row gives for this ref's lookup key' — over a Partial<Record<`${InteractiveRef['k']}:${WidgetIntent['role'] | '*'}`, {…}>>, whose indexed access is {…} | undefined; A-2 then reads suffix.pointers.length off it. The totality that rescues this — a missing key taking { base:'element', pointers: [] }, a specific entry beating '*' — is stated only in the column's // comment, the same standard repair C enforces against renderSuffix two paragraphs earlier. Practical impact is small (an implementer will write the default), but the CI check A-2 declares cannot be written against a lookup no clause declares.
causedByEc22.fix: Declare the lookup beside renderSuffix: `declare function suffixFor(kind: WidgetKind, ref: InteractiveRef, intent: WidgetIntent | null): SuffixSpec;` — returning §4.8.2's entry for `${ref.k}:${intent.role}`, else for `${ref.k}:*`, else the declared default { base: 'element', pointers: [] } — and bind A-2's first argument to `suffixFor(env.kind, ref, ref.k === 'intent' ? resolveInteractive(env, ref) : null)`.

causedByEc22.clause: §0C.14 S0C.32, the EC-2 row (L3215), as amended by repair K — the clause 'which is the case for b35.preview, b35.confirm and a22.configuration, whose resourceClass is SOURCE_HANDOFF'
causedByEc22.consequence: Invalid inference from a CAPABILITY property to an INTENT property. Gate 6's scoping predicate is effect === 'HANDOFF' (S0C.28-quinquies: 'For effect === 'HANDOFF' the subject resolves only the DESTINATION fences'). resourceClass is a C9Capability field and does not determine effect class — the contract's own §0.36 carries appointments.own.reschedule, a SOURCE_HANDOFF key, as a REFINE, and I confirmed in process that 15 of the 56 C9 keys are SOURCE_HANDOFF while only 2 are OWNER_HANDOFF. All three named keys are reachable on non-HANDOFF intents: §2.4 row 7 gives CLIENT_LIST permitted effects NONE/NAVIGATE/REFINE/REQUEST_APPROVAL/HANDOFF with owner keys b35.{preview,status,confirm}, and §0B.7 admits a C9 ref on REFINE, DRAFT, HANDOFF and a class-'c' NAVIGATE — so b35.preview on a REFINE is constructible, and §5646 already describes b35.preview being read for eligibleCount/candidateCount. §2.4 row 16 does the same for a22.configuration on SETTINGS_DRAFT. For every such carriage Gate 6's second C9 branch DOES apply c9Capability's admission on the run-bearing path, so the row understates the fence — safe in direction, but wrong in the one table §0C.32 declares must let a reader 'find every floor reduction it makes by reading this table'.
causedByEc22.fix: Re-key the sentence on effect, and say resourceClass does not imply it. Replace with: '…so for an intent whose EFFECT is 'HANDOFF' that admission is not applied on any path. resourceClass does not determine effect class: b35.preview, b35.confirm and a22.configuration may equally be carried by a REFINE or a class-'c' NAVIGATE (§0B.7), and on those carriages Gate 6's second C9 branch still applies on the run-bearing path.'

causedByEc22.clause: §0C.14 S0C.32, the EC-2 row (L3215), as amended by repair K — 'Their whole fence is therefore c9Floor's C9_MODE_FLOOR/C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR of SESSION_VERIFIED at Gate 5, plus SENSITIVE_DEST and targetFloor('s')'
causedByEc22.consequence: The three named terms are presented as a conjunction ('plus'), and they never all hold at once — the row contradicts EC-4's row two lines below it in the same table. SENSITIVE_DEST is evaluated in exactly one place, FLOOR_EXEMPT's fourth clause (L1786-1788), which requires priority === 0 and target.class === 's'. In that case verificationFloor returns 'ANONYMOUS' outright (L1817-1822), waiving both c9Floor (reached via subjectFloor) and targetFloor — EC-4's own row says so: 'EFFECT_FLOOR, KIND_FLOOR and targetFloor waived for all five; subjectFloor waived for the two class-'s' HANDOFFs only, which floor at ANONYMOUS.' Conversely, for a HANDOFF that is not FLOOR_EXEMPT, c9Floor's SESSION_VERIFIED and targetFloor('s') = SESSION_VERIFIED both apply but SENSITIVE_DEST is never evaluated at all. Concrete failure: SETTINGS_DRAFT's editor_handoff_intent is mandatory, declared priority: 0 (§2.6.16 SETTINGS.4, cited at L1894), a class-'s' HANDOFF, and §2.4 row 16 lists a22.configuration among SETTINGS_DRAFT's owner keys. a22.configuration's WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY consent_class is not personal_data or identity_binding, so SENSITIVE_DEST returns false, FLOOR_EXEMPT is true, and the floor is ANONYMOUS — where the EC-2 row asserts SESSION_VERIFIED. No NEW reduction is created (the ANONYMOUS outcome is EC-4's, and EC-4's row declares it), but the table's EC-2 row now actively asserts a floor its EC-4 row removes, which is precisely the over-read §0C.32 exists to prevent.
causedByEc22.fix: Split the fence by exemption instead of conjoining three terms. Replace the sentence with: 'For a HANDOFF that is not FLOOR_EXEMPT the residual fence is c9Floor's C9_MODE_FLOOR/C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR of SESSION_VERIFIED at Gate 5 together with targetFloor('s'). For a FLOOR_EXEMPT class-'s' HANDOFF — SETTINGS.4's editor_handoff_intent and SOURCE.3's reconnect_intent — EC-4 waives both, and the operative fence is SENSITIVE_DEST's exclusion of consent and identity destinations plus the landing surface's own ingress re-check at EP-FETCH (§0.31); see EC-4's row in this table.' The same correction is owed to S0C.28-quinquies L2825, which is where this three-term list originates.

independentPreExisting.evidence: §2.6.22 declares four rules: ARTIFACT.1 (first-party route), ARTIFACT.2 (minted for one principal), **ARTIFACT.3 — contains_pii is stated before the file is fetched** ('It is a Cell<boolean>; when it is true the text says so in the policy sentence, and pii_ceiling applies'), ARTIFACT.4. §0C.22-nonies declares a different rule under the same identifier: 'ARTIFACT.3 (§2.6.22). fetch_intent is role primary and regenerate_intent is role secondary.' This is the identical defect repair A was written for — a second rule under an existing identifier in a section that governs over §2 by §0C.2, readable as superseding the original — except that here the rule at risk is a PII-disclosure rule and the free number was ARTIFACT.5. The sibling in the same block, APPROVAL.4, is correctly the next free number (§2.6.12 declares APPROVAL.1-3). Introduced by EC-20, not EC-22: the EC-22 diff shows that line as unchanged context, and EC-20's errata row reads 'APPROVAL.4 and ARTIFACT.3 assign the roles the per-control scoping needs.' Not fixed here, per instructions.

const el = resolveInteractive(env, ref) is evaluated BEFORE switch (ref.k) with ref at its full union type, so K infers to the constraint and el is the flat union of all seven element shapes inside every branch. Narrowing ref in a case does not narrow el (TypeScript does not correlate two variables this way), so el.label, el.heading, el.start, el.title and el.row are each member accesses el's declared type does not carry — exactly the failure R6 says the indexed ElementFor was adopted to prevent ('A flat return of the whole union would have nameSourceOf's seven branches reading members the declared type does not carry … so the declaration read as total without type-checking'). Repair B widens that union by a fourth option shape but neither creates nor worsens the correlation problem; the function body is unchanged in the EC-22 diff. Not load-bearing: it defeats a typed-totality claim, not a fence, and the fix is a restructure (bind el inside each case, after ref is narrowed) with no change to any rule.

ProactiveProvenance declares 'moment_template_id: string | null; // REQUIRED iff narrative_source === moment_template' and carries no version member, while MOMENT_TEMPLATES is keyed `${string}@${number}`. PR3b's validator recomputes narrative_hash 'against the template render' and §4.2 replays FROZEN receipts — verbatim the ground repair I gives for adding moment_template_version to Moment and narrative_template_version to MomentTemplate ('§4.2 replays FROZEN receipts, so an id alone cannot resolve'). The same ground applies to this carrier and it was not updated. The defect predates EC-22 (the id@version keying is EC-20's R10), so it is not caused by these repairs, but it is the one reader of the moment-template catalogue left outside repairs I and J's closure. Not load-bearing: a constructibility gap on a NORMATIVE-PENDING proactive path (P-32 is [ABSENT]); it reduces no floor and breaks no fence. Compare §1.6.5's Authorship, which already carries narrative_template_version and therefore resolves.

THIS IS THE STOP CONDITION, and it is the exact defect repair A was written for, left unrepaired one clause above it. §0C.22-nonies declares three new §2 clauses, and I scanned the whole of §0-C for the pattern: exactly three exist — APPROVAL.4 (§2.6.12), ARTIFACT.3 (§2.6.22), CLIENT.3 (§2.6.7). APPROVAL.4 is free: §2.6.12 declares only APPROVAL.1, .2, .3. CLIENT.3 was renumbered by EC-22 precisely to avoid a collision. But §2.6.22 ALREADY DECLARES ARTIFACT.1, ARTIFACT.2, ARTIFACT.3 and ARTIFACT.4 (L4677-4680), and the existing ARTIFACT.3 reads: 'contains_pii is stated before the file is fetched. It is a Cell<boolean>; when it is true the text says so in the policy sentence, and pii_ceiling applies.' The new ARTIFACT.3 reads: 'fetch_intent is role: 'primary' and regenerate_intent is role: 'secondary'.' Two rules, one identifier, and §0C.2 makes §0-C govern on conflict — which is word for word the reading CLIENT.3's own note says 'could be read as superseding that fence, silently deleting it.' The existing ARTIFACT.3 is the clause that makes pii_ceiling apply to the ARTIFACT kind and that requires contains_pii to be disclosed before a file is fetched: a PII clause on the one kind that ships a downloadable file. It appears in neither §0C.13's void table nor §0.17's registers, so nothing else preserves it. Provenance is honest: the collision was created by EC-20 ('APPROVAL.4 and ARTIFACT.3 assign the roles the per-control scoping needs', L3185), not by EC-22 — so it is pre-existing. But EC-22 makes it materially worse in one specific way: by stating the anti-collision doctrine explicitly for CLIENT and applying it to CLIENT alone, repair A licenses the argument e contrario that the ARTIFACT.3 collision was considered and intended to supersede. Minimal fix, which I am not applying: renumber the role clause ARTIFACT.5 and append the same sentence CLIENT.3 carries — '§2.6.22's ARTIFACT.1 … ARTIFACT.4 are unaffected by this section' — and correct the back-reference at L2368 ('Without ARTIFACT.3 the intent:* key …').

independentPreExisting.clause: §0C.14 S0C.32, the enumeration 'Every repair either removes rows from an allowlist (EC-1), adds a veto (EC-7, EC-13), voids an unbuildable claim (EC-8, EC-10, EC-12), declares a carrier that was missing (EC-6, EC-9, EC-14, EC-15), or corrects an identity or a count (EC-3, EC-5, EC-11, EC-16)'
independentPreExisting.evidence: The buckets cover EC-1…EC-16 minus the two floor-reducers, and nothing else. EC-17, EC-18, EC-19, EC-20 and EC-21 all exist as rows in §0C.13 and are classified by no bucket; the fourteen EC-22 repairs add fourteen more. 'Every repair either…' is therefore literally false as an enumeration. Pre-existing: it was already false once EC-17 was added, long before EC-22. NOT load-bearing, because the sentence the enumeration illustrates — 'No repair admits a capability, widens an allowlist, or relaxes a veto' — is unqualified over all repairs and I found no EC-22 repair that violates it: F and L add fences, J tightens a key, G/B/C/D/N are accessible-name composition, A/E/H/I/M are identity and spelling corrections, K is prose in an errata row. Worth one edit ('Every repair through EC-16 either…', or add the later buckets) so the table stops promising an exhaustiveness it does not deliver.

independentPreExisting.clause: §0C.14 S0C.32, the EC-4 row (L3216) — 'The residual is targetFloor('s') on a handoff'
independentPreExisting.evidence: The same cell opens by saying targetFloor is waived for all five exempt intents and closes by calling targetFloor('s') 'the residual'. The intended reading is almost certainly 'the residual RISK is that targetFloor('s') is given up', which the following clause supports ('it is tolerable for a stated reason … a HANDOFF never invokes its destination capability, and §0.31's routes re-check the principal proof at EP-FETCH'). §0C.17's code (L1817-1830) is unambiguous and governs, so nothing is actually at risk. Pre-existing — EC-22 does not touch the EC-4 row — but it is the same ambiguity that repair K then propagated into the EC-2 row, so the two are worth fixing together.

independentPreExisting.clause: §0.17 item 3 (L485) — §2.6.7 CLIENT.2's 'display fence' already downgraded to [NON-NORMATIVE]
independentPreExisting.evidence: 'No display fence is defined in this contract. The normative remainder is pii_ceiling: 'client_identified' plus §0.3's presentation_mode derivation and §2 K18.' Those three do not, between them, refuse a CLIENT_LIST envelope under presentation_mode 'client': §0.11 makes presentation_mode derived rather than proposed, and K18 asserts mode-invariance of kind and of intents[].capability, not a pii_ceiling refusal. The contract CAN express the refusal — §2.6.21 MEDIA.2 does it in one line ('under a client presentation the envelope is refused unless subject_is_principal is true') — so CLIENT.2 could be given a real mechanism by copying MEDIA.2's. NOT load-bearing as it stands: the gap is openly disclosed in §0.17 rather than hidden, and CLIENT_LIST is independently fenced by KIND_FLOOR['CLIENT_LIST'] = SESSION_VERIFIED and by owner classes CLIENT_READ + BULK_AUDIENCE_OWNER, which a client principal does not hold. Recorded here only because question 4 asks whether CLIENT.2 is 'still in force', and the honest answer is: unchanged by EC-22 and in force to exactly the degree §0.17 left it, which is less than its own prose claims.

client2Evidence: §2.6.7 line 4255 still reads verbatim: 'CLIENT.2 This kind is never emitted with presentation_mode: client. Mechanism: pii_ceiling: client_identified combined with the display fence, which refuses client_identified under a client presentation unless the subject is the principal — and a segment is never one principal.' A whole-document search finds exactly three CLIENT.n identifiers: CLIENT.1 and CLIENT.2 in §2.6.7, and CLIENT.3 once, in §0C.22-nonies. The EC-22 diff shows the new rule renumbered from CLIENT.2 to CLIENT.3 in place, with '§2.6.7's CLIENT.1 and CLIENT.2 are unaffected by this section' added in the same edit. There is therefore no reading under which §0-C's precedence over §2 supersedes the pii_ceiling fence: §0-C now declares no rule under the identifier CLIENT.2 at all. (§0.17 item 3 already marks the words 'the display fence' NON-NORMATIVE and states the normative remainder as pii_ceiling 'client_identified' plus §0.3's presentation_mode derivation and §2 K18 — pre-existing, untouched; CLIENT.3's parenthetical only describes CLIENT.2, it does not re-enact it.)

QUESTION 4, answered first and in full. The pii_ceiling 'client_identified' display fence is INTACT and still in force; there is no reading under which §0-C supersedes it. Six independent checks: (1) TEXT UNCHANGED — §2.6.7 line 4255 still reads verbatim 'CLIENT.2 This kind is never emitted with presentation_mode: 'client'. Mechanism: pii_ceiling: 'client_identified' combined with the display fence, which refuses client_identified under a client presentation unless the subject is the principal — and a segment is never one principal. Evaluated at: MINT/VALIDATE.' CLIENT.1 (line 4254) is likewise unchanged. (2) NO IDENTIFIER COLLISION REMAINS — the new role clause is numbered CLIENT.3 (line 2357), so §0-C and §2.6.7 never speak under the same identifier; §0C.2's precedence rule ('where this section CONFLICTS … this section governs') has no conflict to bite on, and 'where it is silent, those documents stand unchanged' applies. (3) EXPLICIT DISCLAIMER — CLIENT.3 states its own reason and then names the survivors: 'Because §0-C governs over §2 (§0C.2), a second rule under the same identifier could be read as superseding that fence, silently deleting it. §2.6.7's CLIENT.1 and CLIENT.2 are unaffected by this section.' That sentence holds on either reading of 'this section' (§0-C.6 or the whole of §0-C), because the only other CLIENT.N anywhere in §0-C is CLIENT.3 itself. (4) NOT VOIDED ANYWHERE ELSE — CLIENT.2 appears in neither §0C.13's void table (twenty rows, EC-1…EC-21) nor §0.17's 'deleted as false against the repository' list (items 17-26); the only §2.6.7 entry in §0.17 is item 3, which predates EC-22. (5) NO DANGLING CITATION — whole-artefact scan of /CLIENT\.[0-9]/ returns exactly three hits: L2357 (CLIENT.3's declaration), L2359 (the disclaimer quoting CLIENT.2), L4255 (CLIENT.2 itself). Nothing cites 'CLIENT.2' expecting the role rule, so the renumbering created no orphan reader. (6) THE FENCE'S DOWNSTREAM CARRIERS ARE UNTOUCHED — §2.4 registry row 7 still carries pii_ceiling client_identified, §2.6.7's registry line still declares it, §4.4.2's retention table still gives CLIENT_LIST '24 h — pii_class client_identified, the shortest window in the contract', and §0.13's KIND_FLOOR still floors CLIENT_LIST at SESSION_VERIFIED. EC-22 changes none of them. ONE PRE-EXISTING CAVEAT, disclosed and not introduced here: §0.17 item 3 had already downgraded the words 'the display fence' inside CLIENT.2 to [NON-NORMATIVE] ('No display fence is defined in this contract. The normative remainder is pii_ceiling: 'client_identified' plus §0.3's presentation_mode derivation and §2 K18'). That downgrade is Section 0's, predates EC-22, and EC-22 neither widens nor narrows it. Repair A therefore did exactly what it was written to do, and the one-line collision that nearly deleted a PII fence is closed — for CLIENT. It was NOT closed for ARTIFACT (see independentPreExisting item 1).
floorReductionEvidence: §0C.32 still carries exactly two rows under 'Two repairs lower a floor' — EC-2 and EC-4 — plus the separate note recording the withdrawal of EC-2's own first-draft floor RAISE. The EC-22 diff touches one cell of the EC-2 row and adds no row, rule or waiver: it replaces 'on the run-bearing path only' with 'on the run-bearing path only AND only where the intent is not a HANDOFF', restating the scoping EC-21 had already effected in §0C.28-quinquies ('for effect === HANDOFF the subject resolves only the DESTINATION fences … never c9Capability's domain/mode admission'). The reduction was made by EC-21; EC-22 only stops the row from over-claiming Gate 6 as a live fence for the three SOURCE_HANDOFF keys. Executed confirmation of the row's key facts: 56 C9 rows; b35.preview [SOURCE_HANDOFF, PROPOSE_ONLY]; b35.confirm [SOURCE_HANDOFF, OWNER_HANDOFF]; a22.configuration [SOURCE_HANDOFF, OWNER_HANDOFF]; c7.measurement.read, c8.result.read, b35.status, owner_report.status, owner_report.download all [SOURCE_READ, READ]; exactly one LOCAL row, c9.no_action.

QUESTION 5: EC-22 creates NO third floor reduction. §0C.32 still declares exactly two (EC-2 and EC-4) and both rows are still there. Positive evidence, by construction: EC-22 edits no floor-producing artefact. c9Floor, C9_MODE_FLOOR, C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR (§0C.10, L1448-1500), subjectFloor (§0B.31), targetFloor / EFFECT_FLOOR / KIND_FLOOR / RISK_FLOOR / CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR (§0.13's table, L174-186), FLOOR_EXEMPT and verificationFloor (§0C.17, L1781-1830) are all byte-identical to their pre-EC-22 form; not one of the fourteen repairs touches them. Of the fourteen, the only ones with any authority direction at all move the fence UP or leave it flat: F adds an EP-MINT refusal where no bulk_intents[] entry matches ref.id; L adds render.render_tier to H1's body_hash term list, so a tier disagreeing with the sealed reading_order now breaks the seal; J tightens both template lookups from a bare id to a composed id@version key; G and B/C/D/N are accessible-name composition only and gate nothing; A, E, H, I, M are identity, pointer-spelling, filter-restatement, carrier and citation corrections. K is the only repair that touches §0C.32 at all, and it edits PROSE IN THE EC-2 ROW — it changes no value verificationFloor can return. The reduction it describes (Gate 6's c9Capability admission not applying to a HANDOFF subject) is EC-21's, already recorded in EC-21's own errata row at L3184; and Gate 6 is an admission test, not a floor — the floor for all three SOURCE_HANDOFF keys remains SESSION_VERIFIED out of c9Floor. Repository facts underlying the EC-2 row re-verified by executing the registry in process (npx ts-node over src/orchestration/c9.registry.ts): C9_CAPABILITIES count = 56; resourceClass = {SOURCE_READ: 40, SOURCE_HANDOFF: 15, LOCAL: 1}; mode = {READ: 41, PROPOSE_ONLY: 13, OWNER_HANDOFF: 2}; LOCAL rows = ['c9.no_action'] (so EC-4's uniqueness assertion holds); OWNER_HANDOFF rows = ['b35.confirm','a22.configuration']; b35.preview = PROPOSE_ONLY/SOURCE_HANDOFF, domains ['CLIENT_LIFECYCLE']; b35.confirm = OWNER_HANDOFF/SOURCE_HANDOFF, domains ['CLIENT_LIFECYCLE']; a22.configuration = OWNER_HANDOFF/SOURCE_HANDOFF, domains ['ADMIN']; b35.status, c7.measurement.read, c8.result.read, owner_report.status, owner_report.download all READ/SOURCE_READ. Every distribution the EC-2 row and §0C.11(1) assert is exact. CAVEAT, and it is why this answer is 'no new reduction' rather than 'the table is clean': repair K's wording makes the EC-2 row ASSERT a floor (SESSION_VERIFIED) for a case where EC-4's row, two lines below in the same table, computes ANONYMOUS — see causedByEc22 item 2. That is a contradiction inside the reduction index, not a third reduction: the ANONYMOUS outcome is EC-4's declared reduction and is findable by reading EC-4's row.
